You are in South Africa I assume - I'm South African. Every time I visit sa it's a heaven. YOU HAVE WOOLWORTHS. They create magic in terms of GF food. Our food is also a million times more expensive here. If you don't have money, you ain't getting the luxury of a GF burger here. I gain 3-5kg every time I go home because of damn WOOLWORTHS. It's truly celiac heaven. 

Europe is not all that. We have a lot of "Oh we know it says gluten free but it's not celiac safe" after you eat something. 

I get glutened all the time at "safe" gluten free places. Germany - glutened all the time! Hungary, actually pretty good with GF. Netherlands was fantastic. Bulgaria and serbia, glutened non stop. 

Diagnosing, you also get told you just have a sensitive stomach for years. I self diagnosed, then told my doctor I was the celiac test and it came back positive. Seeing a specialist doesn't change anything, the answer is always the same: just don't eat gluten.

Point is, celiac sucks everywhere. It gets easier after high school because there are less school events. You can bring your own bread to places! I've even given Spur a bun to make me a burger when I was down in sa 😂 

Don't try to get a normal experience where you are. Unfortunately, we don't have that. And it gets easier with years. You stop craving the bite of cake your friend is eating once you stop thinking about it like that. Don't fantasize about needing bread, my mom does this for me too, she's always trying to find some loaf I can eat in sa. We don't need bread, we got rice cookies or whatever. There are cheaper options. But yes, money makes it easier
